mechanism: exact number-theoretic identity (period-4 in n) + product of three anticommuting Pauli-conditioned pi rotations is a qubit scalar; routing-aware ancilla relocation rewrite (pre-routing, accepted on routed cost)

rule.name: kerr_half_pi_colocate_by_dirty_pauli_triple_rewrite
rule.idea: Replace an ancilla-mediated half-pi Kerr block H(a) CR(pi)(a,m) rx(phi~pi)(a) CR(-pi)(a,m) H(a) [R(k pi)(m)], where the ancilla a is a dirty co-located qubit of m (any state, untouched elsewhere in the window), by a 3-CR dirty-qubit construction: since CR(pi)=(-iZ)^n, A=-iZ,B=-iX,C=-iY satisfy A^n B^n C^n = s(n) a qubit scalar with s(n) period 4, and e^{-i(pi/2)n^2} = R(3pi/2) A^n B^n C^n exactly (verified n mod 4 = 0..3). B^n = H CR(pi) H, C^n = S H CR(pi) H Sdg (time order: C^n acts first), giving sdg,h,CR(pi),h,s,h,CR(pi),h,CR(pi),R(3pi/2+k pi) with the qubit returned to its input state untouched up to the enclosing scalar. All CR gates act on the natively coupled (q_m, m) pair, so routing inserts no SWAPs, trading 2 two-op gates for 3 but removing most ancilla-relocation SWAP overhead. Residual phase error from the angle-tolerant kickback's delta stays within the 1e-6 exact-contract tolerance, matching the admitted parity-kickback rule's own handling of the same delta. Kept only when the routed cost (duration, then 2-op count) decreases versus leaving the original clean-ancilla block in place.
